ai.description: The Yercaud Day Gecko (Gekkonidae) reaches 40 mm SVL. It is brownish-grey with a distinct yellow vertebral stripe and dark lateral spots. Key features include granular scales and a slender, flattened body.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis yercaudensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, bright yellow or orange patch on the throat, which is absent in most other regional congeners.
ai.habitat: *Cnemaspis yercaudensis* inhabits rocky outcrops and tree trunks within the moist deciduous and semi-evergreen forests of the Shevaroy Hills at elevations of 1,200–1,500m.
ai.behavior: The Yercaud Day Gecko is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small insects on rock surfaces and tree trunks during the brightest hours of the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis yercaudensis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, with peak activity observed during the monsoon months.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis yercaudensis* is endemic to the Shevaroy Hills in the Eastern Ghats of Tamil Nadu, India, typically found at elevations between 1,200 and 1,500 meters.
